title_eng: Ideal Filtering Approach on DCT Domain for Biomedical Signals: Index Blocked DCT Filtering Method (IB-DCTFM)
abstract:
We proposed Index-Blocked Discrete Cosine
Transform Filtering Method (IB-DCTFM) to design ideal
frequency range filter on DCT domain for biomedical
signal which frequently exposed to specific frequency noise
such as motion artifacts and 50/60 Hz powerline interfer-
ence. IB-DCTFM removes unwanted frequency range
signal on time domain by blocking specific DCT index on
DCT domain. In simulation, electrocardiography, electro-
myography, photoplethysmography are used as a signal
source and FIR, IIR and adaptive filter are used for
comparison with proposed IB-DCTFM. To evaluate filter
performance, we calculated signal-to-noise ratio and corre-
lation coefficient to clean signal of each signal and filtering
method respectively. As a result of filter simulation,
average signal to noise ration and correlation coefficient
of IB-DCTFM are improved about 75.8 dB/0.477, and FIR,
IIR and adaptive filtering re sults are 24.8 dB/0.130,
54.3 dB/0.440 and 29.5 dB/0.200 respectively.

Ideal Filtering Approach on DCT Domain for Biomedical
Signals: Index Blocked DCT Filtering Method (IB-DCTFM)
Hang Sik Shin & Chungkeun Lee & Myoungho Lee
Received: 17 February 2009 / Accepted: 31 March 2009
# Springer Science + Business Media, LLC 2009
Abstract We proposed Index-Blocked Discrete Cosine
Transform Filtering Method (IB-DCTFM) to design ideal
frequency range filter on DCT domain for biomedical
signal which frequently exposed to specific frequency noise
such as motion artifacts and 50/60 Hz powerline interfer-
ence. IB-DCTFM removes unwanted frequency range
signal on time domain by blocking specific DCT index on
DCT domain. In simulation, electrocardiography, electro-
myography, photoplethysmography are used as a signal
source and FIR, IIR and adaptive filter are used for
comparison with proposed IB-DCTFM. To evaluate filter
performance, we calculated signal-to-noise ratio and corre-
lation coefficient to clean signal of each signal and filtering
method respectively. As a result of filter simulation,
average signal to noise ration and correlation coefficient
of IB-DCTFM are improved about 75.8 dB/0.477, and FIR,
IIR and adaptive filtering re sults are 24.8 dB/0.130,
54.3 dB/0.440 and 29.5 dB/0.200 respectively.
Keywords Discrete cosine transform (DCT) .
Frequency filtering . Powerline interference .
Baseline wandering . Respiration noise
Introduction
Digital filtering is widespread methods to enhance or to
remove the specific frequency range of signals. Actually,
every measured signal is described as an added form of
transmitted (generated) signal and noise. Noise means
every unwanted signal and it corrupts observation and
analysis of signal. To estimate signal clearance, Signal to
Noise (SNR) which means the ratio of a signal power to the
noise power is widely used. Therefore, the most important
meaning of the filtering is the compression of signal noise
power and elevation of SNR. Especially, noise reduction is
very important issue for biomedical signals, because
biomedical signal is a very tiny and has relatively low
SNR ratio because there are many practical difficulties for
biomedical signal acquisition and processing such as
instrumentation effect and physiological artifacts [ 1– 4]. To
improve SNR, time and frequency domain filtering techni-
ques are generally used. In filtering procedure, filter
selection is a most important issue because every signal
generated from different sources such as acoustic, electric,
mechanic, and biomedical origin has different time and
frequency characteristics. Moreover, noise depends on
signal type and acquisition condition. For example, channel
interference, vibration, dispersion, and power line interfer-
ence is a major noise factor of communication signal,
mechanical signal, optical signal, and biomedical signal
respectively. These noises has different characteristic, we
have to consider about optimum filtering method for each
signals.
There are many types of digital filter and signal
conditioning methods for biomedical signal such as finite
impulse response (FIR) filter, infinite impulse response
filter (IIR), adaptive filter, artificial neural network, wavelet
method, and morphological method [ 5– 8]. However, in
considering the most significant noise of biomedical signal
analysis, frequency band filtering method should be
frequently used because most of biomedical noise has its
own frequency range [ 1, 4, 9]. In other words, noise could
be removed from signal by blocking specified frequency

range which corresponds to time domain noise. For
example, power line interference and baseline wandering/
drift could be removed by using 50/60 Hz band stop filter
and high pass filter which has 0.1 Hz cut off frequency,
respectively [ 3, 12– 14].
From the frequency band characteristic of biomedical
signal, frequency band filtering is often used for noise
compression. Conventionally, FIR and IIR filter is widely
used for frequency band filtering. FIR filtering, the most
common filtering method, has a linear phase characteristic
but it has a relatively low noise suppression performance.
On the other hands, IIR filter has a good performance for
noise compression, but non linear phase characteristic of
IIR filter could distort the entire signal. Moreover, IIR filter
has a divergence characteristic and sometimes it cause
system instability [ 1, 3, 10]. Adaptive filtering which is
recently developed method for noise compression shows
the high noise compression ratio assuming we already has
reference signal information. However, the most cases of
signal filtering, it is difficult to obtain a suitable reference
signal [ 16]. Thus adaptive filtering method has a limitation
in filtering biomedical signal.
Considering that one of the most important issues in
filter design is related on how filter discriminate pass-band
and stop-band with accuracy, existing filtering methods has
the limitation of finite pass-band gain and unwanted effect
on circumference frequency bands. On time-domain, ideal
filter which has theoretical infinite pass-band gain cannot
be realized because it needs infinite impulse response.
However, on frequency domain, nevertheless it also has
infinite impulse response in time-domain, we can realize
filter which has ideal frequency characteristic. In this paper,
we propose a novel frequency filtering method using DCT
which removes unwanted frequency range signal by block-
ing specific DCT index on DCT domain for biomedical
signal conditioning and IB-DCTFM has ideal characteris-
tic on frequency domain. Nevertheless there are unavail-
able cases of frequency band filtering such as overlap
signal frequency range with the noise frequency range,
most of common biomedical interference such as power
line interference, baseline wand ering/drift, and respiration
effect resides on specific frequency range and it could be
removed with frequency band filtering [ 9]. Therefore we
designed a noise model which is frequently occurred in
biomedical analysis and simulated the proposed filter
performance with SNR and correlation coefficient. To
evaluate of proposed filter performance, FIR, IIR and
adaptive filter method are also used to noise removal and
to compare with simulation result of proposed filter as a
comparative methods. Moreover, we considered signal
distortion such Gibbs phenomenon which is caused by
infinite impulse response characteristic of IB-DCTFM and
IIR filtering for practical use.

Materials and methods
DCT filter characteristics
A discrete cosine transform convert a finite discrete sequence
data to a sum of cosine function with different frequencies. For
frequency domain analysis, Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT)
is the most widely used method. However, DFT is not proper
in quantitative frequency filtering because it returns the
transform result with a complex value, but on the other hand
DCT returns a real value as a result and it is more suitable to
handle a frequency domain data directly. Equation 1 shows
general DCT equation which transform time domain signal to
frequency domain signal based on sum of cosine functions
oscillating at different frequencies:
